task_name: Anvil and Oak Strength - Movement coaching clip library
client_brief:
Anvil and Oak is not ready to cut the full coaching library yet: our demo pack does not carry a complete repetition in every angle we need, and we are not going to loop a take to pretend otherwise. What we need from you now is the launch package that puts the library in front of subscribers. Cut it short, cut it silent or to the bed we supply, and put the coaching on screen as text, because a lifter under a bar watches with the sound off. The movement names and the cues must read exactly as they are written in the cleared library sheet, and the framing and the lifter must agree across all three films: wherever a movement appears in more than one film, each film shows it with the same lifter, filmed from the same camera position.

Final handoff
1. Movement library launch reel: 1 named export, 16:9, 12 to 15 seconds, instrumental bed only, no speech. All six cleared movement names appear as on screen text, and at least one movement carries its cue line: the Conventional Deadlift carries the sixth cue of its row in the library sheet, the cue for the pull from the floor, over one complete repetition of the lift. The wordmark and the certification seal recovered from the patch photograph appear together at least once.
2. Vertical library cutdown: 1 named export, 9:16, 8 to 9 seconds, silent, no audio track at all. The barbell stays inside the frame for every repetition shown, and one movement on screen carries a cue line from its own row of the library sheet, set over the action that cue describes.
3. Square library cutdown: 1 named export, 1:1, 6 to 8 seconds, silent, no audio track at all. One movement on screen carries a cue line from its own row of the library sheet, set over one complete repetition of that movement, and the wordmark closes the film.

The per movement demonstrations we asked for previously are withdrawn from this commission and will be re briefed once the source pack carries full coverage.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.
- Video delivery means a playable MP4, not a storyboard, still montage PDF or editing log. Every film in this package is silent or carries the supplied instrumental bed only. There is no narration, no voice over and no spoken claim: the message is carried by on screen text that you set.
- Every supplied clip runs about five seconds. Each film must cut together at least three different supplied video takes, and no film may be padded by looping, freezing or slowing a single clip to reach its runtime.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.typography: Anvil and Oak Strength runs Trade Gothic for display and Benton Sans for text. Step 01, Display / H1, is Trade Gothic Bold Condensed No. 20 capitals at 96 px on 60 px leading, tracking -0.01 em, carrying movement names on the wide reel, for example ROMANIAN DEADLIFT forced onto two flush left rows, the leading being 0.86 of the 70 px cap height, with a 3 px Ember Rust rule under the lower row at that row's exact width, and 34 pt on 21 pt on the printed card. Step 02, Subheading / H2, is the same face at 72 px on 45 px leading, tracking -0.01 em, for the square cutdown, for example FRONT SQUAT, again on two rows under the rust rule. Step 03, Body, is Benton Sans Medium 500 at 48 px on 67 px leading, tracking 0, max 65 characters, carrying coaching cues at 1.4 spacing, 56 px on 78 px in the vertical cutdown and 10.5 pt on 15 pt in print. Step 04, Fine print, is Benton Sans Medium 500 at 28 px on 38 px leading, tracking +0.04 em, numerals tabular lining, 8 pt on 11 pt in print. A movement name is never set on one line.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, instructional and calm. Speaks like a coach giving a cue, not a brand selling one. Example line: 'Brace, hinge, drive through the floor. That is the whole lift.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The wordmark and the in house certification seal survive only as stitching on a canvas gym bag patch, held now as one handheld photograph. Both have to be recovered from that photograph as artwork before they can go on the cards and the library sheet. The seal is a compound ring lockup, type set around a central anvil glyph inside a ruled ring. There is no vector file, no colour spec and no prior guideline.
brand_identity.values: Competence and honesty: real bodies doing real work, taught by people who actually lift.
brand_identity.signature_type_move: Every movement name is forced onto two lines whatever its length, flush left with leading at 0.86 of the cap height so the rows almost touch, and a 3 px Ember Rust rule pinned under the lower line at exactly that line's width.

palette_rules.distribution: Grounds and panels are Chalk, Whitewash Wall or Anvil Iron and nothing else; Chalk is the main light ground, as on anvil_oak_exercise_card_2025.pdf. On Chalk or Whitewash Wall, movement names, cues, the “STRENGTH” line and the seal are Anvil Iron, the wordmark “ANVIL & OAK” is Oak, and secondary lines and fine print are Anvil Iron or Steel Grey, as on the card. On Anvil Iron, all type, the wordmark and the seal are Chalk or Whitewash Wall. Ember Rust is the 3 px rule under each movement name and nothing else. All designed type, the wordmark and the seal sit on a solid ground or panel, never straight on footage, as the card keeps its type off the photograph. Ember Rust and Steel Grey together cover no more than 5% of the designed, non-footage area of any frame.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow, glow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, type, rule, the wordmark or the seal, and no scrim, gradient, vignette or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over the footage: a name or cue over a shot sits on a solid Chalk, Whitewash Wall or Anvil Iron panel. Cuts and short dissolves between shots are transitions, not tints; colour and opacity are judged on a settled frame.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the six palette hexes for type, panels, rules, icons, the wordmark or the seal, pure white #FFFFFF and pure black included. No glow, drop shadow, gradient, bevel, outline or metallic effect on any type, rule, panel, the wordmark or the seal. No Ember Rust type, ground, panel or icon.
palette_rules.photography: The supplied takes keep their own colour and are never recoloured toward the palette: the whitewashed board wall in the footage stays as it was shot, not tinted to Whitewash Wall or Chalk, no take is warmed toward Oak or Ember Rust, and any correction only neutralises a colour cast.
